linkedin:
Only 22% of remote job listings show a pay figure—the other 78% are marked DOE, and you have to guess the USD salary. Here is how to handle it.

DOE (determined on experience) means the employer sets your pay after reviewing your resume, skills, and market value. It is not always a red flag. Companies use it to stay flexible and to tailor pay to seniority, especially in fields like AI and specialized healthcare where skills vary widely.

From Loker Dollar's analysis of 4,280 active remote listings:
- 940 (22%) state a concrete USD figure; 3,340 (78%) leave pay blank
- 2,735 (64%) accept applicants from any country
- 1,213 listings posted in the last 7 days

A hidden number can be a negotiation lever. Anchor with the high end of the market range you researched, quantify your impact with concrete metrics, and ask about total compensation—benefits, equity, and bonuses can close the gap.

Read the full breakdown: https://lokerdollar.com/en/blog/what-is-doe-wage
